name: Pat Stryker
current_role: Founder and president, Bohemian Foundation (Fort Collins, Colorado)
profile: Granddaughter of Stryker Corp. founder Homer Stryker; her fortune comes from inherited Stryker stock. Based in Fort Collins, she founded the Bohemian Foundation in 2001 (music, community, global and civic programs), has given ~$225M to charity, redevelops downtown Fort Collins real estate and is a major Democratic donor.
interesting_fact: In 2016 she and her brother Jon Stryker gave a combined $10M to fund the first US memorial to victims of racial-terror lynchings; she is also counted among Colorado's political 'Gang of Four' donors with Tim Gill, Jared Polis and Rutt Bridges.
deep_cut_fact: She once owned a California winery, Stryker Sonoma, which she sold to focus on the foundation; the foundation built The Music District, a creative hub and workspace for Fort Collins musicians, and was named after the Paris Bohemian movement of the early 1900s.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. Best route is the Bohemian Foundation (262 E. Mountain Ave, Fort Collins; main office line published on its contact page). Music/Fort Collins community angle is the natural hook.

name: Rajendrakumar Shivkisan Agrawal
current_role: Director, Haldiram Foods International (Nagpur Haldiram's) and related family companies; shareholder in merged Haldiram Snacks Food Pvt Ltd
profile: Member of the Nagpur branch of the Haldiram's snack-food family; Indian company registries list him as a director of Haldiram Foods International and some 27 related companies. The family's fortune jumped after the Delhi and Nagpur businesses merged in 2025 into Haldiram Snacks Food (Nagpur ~44%) and Temasek, Alpha Wave and IHC bought stakes at a reported ~$10B valuation.
interesting_fact: Haldiram's traces back to Ganga Bhishen 'Haldiram' Agarwal's bhujia shop in Bikaner; the Nagpur arm was built by Shivkisan Agrawal, who introduced kaju katli to Nagpur. Hurun named Rajendrakumar one of India's biggest wealth gainers in its 2026 Global Rich List.
notes: Almost no public profile, interviews or social accounts found. Sources call him part of the Nagpur Haldiram family but don't state the exact relation; the patronymic 'Shivkisan' suggests he is a son of Nagpur founder-chairman Shivkisan Agrawal, but that is unverified. The only email on the Haldiram's Nagpur site is customer support (support@haldirams.com), so it's a poor route. Corporate PR via Haldiram Snacks Food is likely better.

name: Cameron Adams
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Canva
profile: Sydney-based designer-engineer who co-founded Canva in 2012 with Melanie Perkins and Cliff Obrecht and leads product, design and technical development. Before Canva he ran a design agency, spent four years at Google as the designer on Google Wave, and co-founded an email startup (Fluent) with other ex-Googlers. Canva was valued at $42B in 2025.
interesting_fact: He was the lone designer on Google Wave, working with Google Maps co-founders Lars and Jens Rasmussen; Lars Rasmussen later introduced him to Melanie Perkins, and he was recruited as an adviser before signing on as Canva's third co-founder.
deep_cut_fact: Long before Canva he blogged as 'The Man in Blue' and wrote about a 'resolution dependent layout' technique, a forerunner of responsive web design; he has written five books on web design, and he still publishes a year-end DJ mix of the best songs of each year on his site.
notes: Approachable and publicly invites contact on his site about startups, technology, design and speaking (the email address dates from 2018, so it may be stale). He does many podcasts (First Round, Lenny's). The LinkedIn handle comes from a mirrored post and is unverified.

name: John Fisher
current_role: Managing partner/owner, the Athletics (MLB); Executive Vice Chairman, Pisces Inc.; co-founder, Sansome Partners
profile: Youngest son of Gap founders Donald and Doris Fisher; his fortune comes mainly from his Gap stake (he left Gap's board in 2022). He co-founded the family investment office Sansome Partners in 1997 and controls the Athletics, which moved from Oakland to Sacramento and are building a ~$1.75B domed ballpark on the Las Vegas Strip (target 2028), with his family pledging about $1B.
interesting_fact: Fisher is a long-time education reformer: he chairs the KIPP Foundation board of the charter school network, and his family committed about $1 billion of equity to the Las Vegas ballpark.
deep_cut_fact: He helped found the Charter School Growth Fund and the Silicon Schools Fund and still serves on both boards; he earned his Princeton degree in politics before getting a Stanford MBA.
notes: He rarely does interviews, except on the Vegas stadium (e.g. LVSportsBiz). Media requests go through the A's Baseball Communications department; no media email is published, only the main team line on the Contact the A's page. A sensitive topic: he is unpopular with Oakland fans over the relocation, so avoid it in outreach.

name: Patrice Motsepe
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, African Rainbow Minerals; President, Confederation of African Football (CAF, re-elected 2025)
profile: South African lawyer-turned-mining entrepreneur and the first Black African on the Forbes billionaires list (2008). He was the first Black partner at Bowman Gilfillan (1994), then bought marginal gold shafts in 1997 and built African Rainbow Minerals. He also founded African Rainbow Capital, has a stake in Sanlam, owns Mamelodi Sundowns and has led CAF since 2021.
interesting_fact: In 2013 he became the first African to sign the Giving Pledge. His Mamelodi Sundowns have won the South African Premiership every season since 2017-18.
deep_cut_fact: His first business, Future Mining, was a contract-mining outfit that cleaned gold dust from inside the Vaal Reefs mine shafts, paying workers a low base salary plus a profit-sharing bonus. He learned business as a boy in his father's spaza shop, which served mine workers.
notes: ARM lists Betty Maloka (Senior Manager: Media Relations and Brand Management) as its media contact. Very high-profile and press-friendly; mining, energy and African-investment angles fit the podcast. He is the subject of 2026 speculation about a run for the ANC presidency.

name: Tim Cook
current_role: Executive Chairman, Apple (stepped down as CEO on Sept 1, 2026, succeeded by John Ternus); director, Nike
profile: Alabama-raised industrial engineer who joined Apple in 1998 from Compaq, after 12 years at IBM, to fix its supply chain. As COO he became Steve Jobs's successor and was CEO from 2011 to Aug 2026, taking Apple to record valuations. He is one of the few billionaires who made his fortune as a hired CEO. As executive chairman he now focuses partly on global policy engagement.
interesting_fact: He handed the CEO role to hardware chief John Ternus on Sept 1, 2026 after nearly 15 years. He came from humble roots (his father was a shipyard worker, his mother worked at a pharmacy) and was salutatorian of Robertsdale High School in 1978.
deep_cut_fact: To pay his way through Auburn's industrial-engineering program he did a co-op with Reynolds Aluminum, working in Richmond, Virginia every other quarter. Before Apple he was COO of the computer-reseller division of Intelligent Electronics.
notes: The press contact is Josh Rosenstock, named on Apple's Cook/Ternus transition release. Very hard to book; any request goes through Apple PR. The X handle @tim_cook is widely known, but I didn't confirm it on the leadership page. The Intelligent Electronics detail is sourced to Wikipedia/CNN Fast Facts.

name: Amy Goldman Fowler
current_role: Co-owner, Solil Management (Goldman family real estate); author, heirloom gardener and seed-conservation philanthropist
profile: Daughter of New York real estate investor Sol Goldman, she shares ownership of Solil Management (about 400 properties) equally with her siblings; her sister Jane runs it. She holds a Ph.D. in clinical psychology, grows heirloom vegetables on her Rhinebeck, NY farm, has written five books, and is a former board chair and now special adviser of Seed Savers Exchange.
interesting_fact: Her husband Cary Fowler helped create the Svalbard Global Seed Vault. Her books (The Melon, The Heirloom Tomato, The Compleat Squash, Heirloom Harvest) have won multiple American Horticultural Society Book of the Year awards.
deep_cut_fact: She also sculpts: 'Rare Forms' is her line of limited-edition bronze sculptures of heirloom produce from her Hudson Valley garden. Garden Conservancy president emeritus Gregory Long called her 'perhaps the world's premier vegetable gardener.'
notes: Her author website has a contact page and a media kit. The best hook is gardening, seed conservation and books rather than real estate. She publishes as 'Amy Goldman'.

name: Siew Khim Ng
current_role: Unknown; listed by Hurun as a billionaire whose wealth derives from Indoritel (Indonesia)
profile: Hurun Global Rich List (2023-2026) attributes about $3B to Siew Khim Ng via Indoritel Makmur Internasional (IDX: DNET), the listed parent of the Indomaret convenience-store chain and a holder of FiberStar. I found no public source that names her role or shareholding. DNET's disclosed major holders are Hannawell Group Ltd (~39%), Anthoni Salim (~25%) and PT Megah Eraraharja (~20%).
interesting_fact: Indomaret, which Indoritel controls, runs more than 21,900 convenience stores across 32 Indonesian provinces.
notes: Identity unresolved: the only web profiles named 'Siew Khim Ng' are unrelated executives at Malaysia's U Mobile and Singapore's Keong Hong. She may be the beneficial owner behind the offshore holder Hannawell Group, but that is unverified. Very private. If you approach her, go through Indoritel corporate secretary/IR.

name: J. Hyatt Brown
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Brown & Brown, Inc. (NYSE: BRO)
profile: Born in 1937 and raised in Daytona Beach, he became CEO in 1961 of the insurance agency his father co-founded in 1939 and grew it into Brown & Brown, one of the largest US insurance brokerages (2025 revenue above $5.9B). His son J. Powell Brown has been CEO since 2009; Hyatt remains chairman and owns about 12% of the company.
interesting_fact: He served in the Florida House from 1972 to 1980, including as Speaker (1978-80). The Cici and Hyatt Brown Museum in Daytona Beach, which he and his wife funded with $13M, holds the world's largest collection of Florida art.
deep_cut_fact: In 2018 he and his wife Cici gave Stetson University $18M, the largest gift in the school's history (he is a past chairman of Stetson's trustees). That same year they pledged $15M to rebuild Daytona Beach's Riverfront Park.

public_contacts.value: Brown & Brown PR: Jenny Goco, VP Public Relations & Communications (phone published in press releases; no email listed)

notes: He is 89. The best route is Brown & Brown corporate communications (Jenny Goco) or the Brown Museum / Museum of Arts and Sciences in Daytona Beach. He is also a director of Daytona International Speedway LLC.

name: Ugo Gussalli Beretta
current_role: Board member, Beretta Holding (retired from executive roles in 2015; former chairman of Fabbrica d'Armi Pietro Beretta and president of Beretta USA)
profile: 14th-generation head of Beretta, the world's oldest firearms maker (founded 1526 in Gardone Val Trompia, Italy). He rose from general manager to CEO to chairman, then handed day-to-day control to his sons Pietro (Beretta Holding) and Franco (Fabbrica d'Armi Pietro Beretta). In 2026 he joined the family's 500th-anniversary celebrations.
interesting_fact: Beretta's first recorded deal was the sale of 185 arquebus barrels to the Republic of Venice in 1526. The company marked its 500th anniversary in 2026 with events attended by Italian PM Giorgia Meloni and a commemorative stamp.
deep_cut_fact: Under his leadership Beretta decided in 1977 to manufacture in the US, buying the former Firearms International factory in Accokeek, Maryland; the first US-made product was the M950 pistol. He was featured in American Rifleman's March 1980 article on the company.
notes: He is about 89, retired and private. Approach through Beretta Holding corporate communications or his sons; Pietro Gussalli Beretta is the public face. The contacts page is JavaScript-rendered and no email could be extracted.

name: Henry Lee Hillman
profile: Henry Lea Hillman (1918-2017) was the Pittsburgh billionaire investor and philanthropist who chaired The Hillman Company, his family's investment office, and the Hillman Family Foundations. He died on April 14, 2017.
notes: Deceased: died April 14, 2017 (CBS Pittsburgh / Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, cited on Wikipedia). The input name 'Henry Lee Hillman' is a variant of Henry Lea Hillman (Forbes 1996 list). The family office (The Hillman Company) and Hillman Family Foundations continue.

name: Zhang Xin
current_role: Founder, Closer Media (film production/finance); CEO, Closer Properties / Closer Group family office (New York); co-founder of SOHO China (resigned 2022)
profile: Born in Beijing in 1965, she worked in Hong Kong factories as a teen, then studied at Sussex and Cambridge and worked at Barings and Goldman Sachs. In 1995 she co-founded SOHO China with her husband Pan Shiyi and built it into Beijing's leading office developer. She has since moved her base to the US, investing in Manhattan trophy buildings (Park Avenue Plaza, a stake in the GM Building) and, since 2021, film through Closer Media.
interesting_fact: She won a special prize at the 2002 Venice Architecture Biennale as a patron for Commune by the Great Wall, a collection of villas by 12 Asian architects. In 2026 she was invited into the Executives Branch of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.
deep_cut_fact: To pay her way in England as a student she worked in a traditional fish-and-chip shop run by a Chinese couple. Years later she made a cameo as a Chinese investor in Oliver Stone's 'Wall Street: Money Never Sleeps' (2010).
notes: Shares her fortune with her husband Pan Shiyi. She is a frequent speaker (WEF, Aspen trustee, MoMA trustee) and fairly media-friendly; film, architecture and US real estate are good hooks. No published email was found. My web-search budget ran out at this point, so contacts beyond her company sites were not checked.

name: James Dinan
current_role: Founder and former chairman/CEO, York Capital Management; co-owner, Milwaukee Bucks; runs his family office
profile: Baltimore-born, Wharton/Harvard MBA hedge-fund manager who started York Capital in 1991 with $3.6M raised from former DLJ colleagues and grew it into a ~$20B event-driven/merger-arbitrage firm. He stepped back as York wound down outside capital and left the chairmanship in late 2023; he now manages his family office and co-owns the Milwaukee Bucks (since 2014).
interesting_fact: He lost his entire $600,000 in savings in the 1987 Black Monday crash, then founded York Capital four years later; the fund made its name with a 33.8% return in 1993.
deep_cut_fact: York Capital is named after York Avenue, the Manhattan street he lived on when he started it. After his large gift to Penn in 2024, Wharton's Vance Hall was renamed Dinan Hall.
notes: Private. The only public route found is York Capital (its site blocked automated access, so no contact could be checked); the Bucks front office is an alternative. His profile appears in the book 'Merger Masters: Tales of Arbitrage' (Columbia UP, 2018), useful background for outreach.

name: Zhang Bangxin
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, TAL Education Group (NYSE: TAL)
profile: Beijing-based founder (born ~1981; Sichuan University, Peking University, CEIBS) who co-founded TAL Education in 2003 as a K-12 after-school tutoring business. TAL listed on the NYSE in 2010. After China's 2021 crackdown on for-profit tutoring it pivoted toward learning devices, enrichment and the overseas Think Academy brand (US, UK, Canada, Australia, Singapore).
interesting_fact: TAL stands for 'Tomorrow Advancing Life' (好未来). In 2018 the company bought CodeMonkey, an Israeli platform that teaches children to code.
deep_cut_fact: He started out as a maths tutor: Bloomberg's 2018 profile was headlined 'Raging Demand for Tutoring Makes Math Teacher a Billionaire'. He co-founded TAL in August 2003 with Cao Yundong.
notes: Low public profile in Western media. TAL IR contact: Jackson Ding (Oct 2026 earnings release). Education technology and AI learning devices are the relevant hooks. The deep-cut fact relies on the Bloomberg headline only; my web-search budget was exhausted, so it was not checked further.
